answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require a 100-token bond locked for 30 days and three independent audits before voting weight activates. Each added identity raises the bond by 25% and adds one audit round, so a coordinated attack has increasing marginal cost. Random peers verify signed task receipts; failure slashes the bond and freezes rewards. This anchor makes a zenith of cloned accounts costly, while a willow-like record lets honest agents prove their work.
